서점.x: I bought a Korean book at the bookstore.
서점.e: Literally 'book store'. -점 = store, as in 편의점 (convenience store).

아래.t: 아래 and 밑 are often interchangeable; 밑 suggests directly underneath.

어깨.x: My shoulders hurt from using the computer too long.

의사.x: My older sister is a doctor who works at a hospital.
의사.t: When speaking to a doctor, call them 선생님 or 의사 선생님.

의사.m: righteous patriot, martyr (who resisted with arms)
의사.ex: 안중근 의사는 하얼빈에서 이토 히로부미를 저격했어요.
의사.x: The patriot Ahn Jung-geun shot Ito Hirobumi in Harbin.
의사.t: Homonym: 의사 also means a doctor; 안중근 의사 means the patriot, not a physician.

쓰다.forms: 써요 · 썼어요 · 쓸 거예요 · 쓰세요 (ㅡ drops)
쓰다.x: I wrote a letter to my friend.
쓰다.t: 쓰다 also means 'to use', 'to wear (a hat/glasses)' and 'to be bitter' — context tells you which.

쓰다.forms: 써요 · 썼어요 · 쓸 거예요 · 쓰세요 (ㅡ drops)
쓰다.t: 돈을 쓰다 = to spend money. 사용하다 is a more formal synonym.

쓰다.forms: 써요 · 썼어요 · 쓸 거예요 · 쓰세요 (ㅡ drops)
쓰다.m: to wear, to put on (hat, glasses, mask); to hold up (umbrella)
쓰다.x: It was raining outside, so I used an umbrella.
쓰다.e: For the head and face: 모자/안경/마스크를 쓰다; 우산을 쓰다 = hold an umbrella.
쓰다.t: Korean has different 'wear' verbs: 입다 clothes, 신다 shoes/socks, 쓰다 hats/glasses/masks.
Same spelling as the verb 쓰다 'to write, to use, to wear (a hat)' — context tells you which.

요금.x: Last month's electric bill was high.
요금.t: Use 요금 for services like buses, phones and utilities; use 가격 for the price of goods.

눈물.x: The movie was so sad that I teared up.

여가.ex: 주말 여가 시간에 보통 뭐 하세요?
여가.x: What do you usually do in your free time on weekends?
여가.e: Literally 'leftover leisure' — time left over after work.
여가.t: Usually appears as 여가 시간 (free time) or 여가 활동 (leisure activities).

비밀번호.ex: 비밀번호를 잊어버려서 새 비밀번호를 다시 만들었어요.
비밀번호.x: I forgot my password, so I made a new one.
비밀번호.t: Often shortened to 비번 in casual speech.

뛰다.m: to run; to jump; to beat (heart)
뛰다.x: I ran to the bus stop because I was afraid of missing the bus.
뛰다.e: Also the heart: 가슴이 뛰다 = my heart is pounding.

다른.ex: 죄송한데 이 옷은 다른 색깔도 있어요?
다른.x: Excuse me, does this come in another color?
다른.e: Modifier form of 다르다 'to be different'.
다른.t: For 'different', use 다르다, not 틀리다, which means 'wrong'.

위치.ex: 이 호텔은 위치가 좋아서 지하철역에서 가까워요.
위치.x: This hotel has a good location, so it's close to the subway station.
위치.e: Literally 'the place where something is put'.

의견.ex: 이 문제에 대해 여러분의 의견을 말해 주세요.
의견.x: Please share your opinions on this issue.

그게.x: Well, the thing is… I actually forgot.
그게.e: Contraction of 그것이 'that (thing)' + the subject marker 이.
그게.t: Used when you hesitate before explaining something awkward. Literal use is common too: 그게 뭐예요? 'What's that?'

신체.ex: 규칙적인 운동은 신체 건강에 도움이 돼요.
신체.x: Regular exercise is good for your physical health.
신체.e: Literally 'body-body'; a formal word for the human body.
신체.t: 신체 is formal and written; in everyday conversation just say 몸.

기념하다.x: To mark my graduation, I took photos with my family.
기념하다.t: 기념하다 marks an event; 축하하다 congratulates a person on it.

가요.ex: 저는 요즘 한국 가요를 들으면서 한국어를 공부해요.
가요.x: These days I study Korean while listening to Korean pop songs.
가요.e: Literally 'songs and ballads.' Don't confuse it with 가요 'I go.'
가요.t: K-pop is often called 가요 in Korea; 케이팝 is used more when talking about it internationally.

배려.x: Being considerate of other people is important.
배려.e: Literally 'sharing out your concern' to others.

변화.ex: 지난 10년 동안 이 동네에 큰 변화가 있었어요.
변화.x: This neighborhood has changed a lot over the past ten years.

쓸쓸하다.x: It feels a bit lonely when I eat dinner alone.
쓸쓸하다.t: 외롭다 is about missing people; 쓸쓸하다 also describes empty, bleak places or late autumn.

전환.x: Taking a walk is good for refreshing your mood.
전환.t: 기분 전환 'a change of pace, refreshing yourself' is the most common collocation.

후반.ex: 축구 경기 후반에 우리 팀이 골을 넣었어요.
후반.x: Our team scored a goal in the second half of the soccer game.
후반.t: Often used with ages: 20대 후반 means 'late twenties'.

수수하다.ex: 그 배우는 평소에 수수한 옷을 즐겨 입어요.
수수하다.x: That actor usually likes to wear plain clothes.
수수하다.e: Positive nuance: unflashy and modest, unlike 촌스럽다 'tacky'.

대신하다.m: to replace, take the place of, stand in for
대신하다.ex: 오늘은 제가 김 선생님을 대신해서 수업을 할게요.
대신하다.x: Today I'll teach the class in place of Mr. Kim.
대신하다.e: Literally 'replace the body' — standing in for someone.

철저하다.x: You have to prepare thoroughly before the exam.

채팅방.x: I'll post the meeting place in the chat room.
채팅방.t: Join or leave: 채팅방에 들어가다 / 채팅방을 나가다; invite someone: 채팅방에 초대하다. Casually also 톡방.

재학생.ex: 이 도서관은 재학생만 이용할 수 있어요.
재학생.x: Only current students can use this library.

수강 신청.m: course registration, signing up for classes
수강 신청.ex: 수강 신청 날에는 인기 과목이 몇 분 만에 마감돼요.
수강 신청.x: On registration day, popular classes fill up in a few minutes.
수강 신청.t: Students jokingly call the scramble for seats 수강 신청 전쟁, 'the registration war'.

고체.x: When water freezes, it becomes ice, which is a solid.

전류.ex: 젖은 손으로 만지면 전류가 흘러서 위험해요.
전류.x: If you touch it with wet hands, current can flow through you, which is dangerous.
전류.t: Pronounced [절류]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

스팸.ex: 하루에도 스팸 문자가 몇 개씩 와요.
스팸.x: I get several spam texts every day.
스팸.e: From English 'spam'; the canned meat is also hugely popular in Korea as a holiday gift set.

감탄.x: The tourists marveled at the beautiful scenery.
감탄.e: Literally 'feel and sigh' — the 'wow' you let out at something amazing.

겁먹다.forms: 겁먹어요 · 겁먹었어요 · 겁먹을 거예요 · 겁먹지 마세요
겁먹다.m: to get scared, to be intimidated
겁먹다.ex: 큰 개를 보고 아이가 겁먹어서 울었어요.
겁먹다.x: The child got scared when he saw the big dog and cried.
겁먹다.e: 겁 'fear' + 먹다 'to eat' — literally 'to eat fear'.
겁먹다.t: Pronounced [검먹따]; 겁먹지 마 'Don't be scared' is a common reassurance.

오만하다.x: Even after he succeeded, he wasn't arrogant.
오만하다.t: 오만 alone can also mean 50,000; context tells you which.

부디.m: please, I sincerely hope, by all means
부디.x: Please take good care of yourself and stay well.
부디.t: Heartfelt and formal, used in wishes and farewells; 제발 sounds more pleading.

이리저리.forms: 이리저리 + movement verb: 이리저리 다니다, 이리저리 찾다
이리저리.m: here and there, this way and that
이리저리.x: I ran here and there trying to find my lost key.

말하자면.m: so to speak, in a way, as it were
말하자면.ex: 그 사람은 말하자면 우리 팀의 엄마 같은 존재예요.
말하자면.x: She's, so to speak, like the mom of our team.
말하자면.e: From 말하다 'to say' + -자면 'if one is to': 'if I were to put it'.
말하자면.t: Often softened with 굳이: 굳이 말하자면 'if I had to say'.

분리하다.m: to separate, to divide, to split
분리하다.x: You have to separate your trash by type before throwing it out.
분리하다.t: Pronounced [불리하다] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

차단하다.m: to block, to cut off, to shut out
차단하다.t: Also for blocking someone online: 번호를 차단하다, 사이트를 차단하다.

무난하다.ex: 면접에는 무난한 색의 옷을 입는 게 좋아요.
무난하다.x: It's best to wear safe-colored clothes to an interview.
무난하다.t: It means 'fine, no problems' — neither great nor bad: 무난하게 합격하다 (to pass comfortably).

미미하다.x: The effect of this policy is still minimal.

촘촘하다.ex: 이 그물은 아주 촘촘해서 작은 물고기도 잡을 수 있어요.
촘촘하다.x: This net is so fine that it can catch even small fish.
촘촘하다.e: The doubled syllable suggests many small things packed closely together.

모순.x: There's a contradiction between what he says and what he does.
모순.e: From an old tale: a seller praising both an unstoppable spear and an unbreakable shield.

줄다리기.x: Our class won the tug-of-war at the school sports day.
줄다리기.e: 줄 'rope' + 다리기, from an old verb meaning 'to pull' (now 당기다).
줄다리기.t: A staple of school sports days (운동회). Also used figuratively for a tug-of-war between two sides, as in negotiations.

리얼리티.ex: 요즘은 연애 리얼리티 프로그램이 인기가 많아요.
리얼리티.x: Dating reality shows are very popular these days.
리얼리티.t: Usually followed by 프로그램 or 쇼. 관찰 예능 'observational variety' is a related genre that follows celebrities' daily lives. On its own it often means 'realism': 리얼리티가 떨어지다 = to feel unrealistic.

콩닥콩닥.ex: 좋아하는 사람을 보니까 가슴이 콩닥콩닥 뛰어요.
콩닥콩닥.x: Seeing the person I like makes my heart go thump-thump.
콩닥콩닥.e: Also the sound of grain being pounded in a mortar; today it's mostly used for a heart beating fast.
콩닥콩닥.t: The verb is 콩닥거리다. It sounds lighter and cuter than 두근두근, often for a crush.

땡땡이를 치다.forms: 땡땡이를 쳤어요 · 땡땡이를 치지 마세요 · 땡땡이치다
땡땡이를 치다.m: to skip class or work, to play hooky
땡땡이를 치다.ex: 날씨가 좋아서 친구랑 수업 땡땡이를 쳤어요.
땡땡이를 치다.x: The weather was nice, so I skipped class with a friend.
땡땡이를 치다.e: 땡땡이 means slacking off or sneaking away from one's duties; 치다 is the verb it pairs with. The origin of 땡땡이 is unclear.
땡땡이를 치다.t: Casual. For skipping without permission; neutral alternatives: 수업을 빼먹다, 수업에 빠지다.

자아.x: In adolescence, people struggle a lot to find themselves.
자아.e: Literally 'self-I' — the 'I' that is aware of itself.

의리.ex: 그 친구는 의리가 있어서 어려울 때 꼭 도와줘요.
의리.x: That friend is loyal, so he always helps when things are tough.
의리.t: 의리 is a prized value in Korean friendships: sticking by someone through hard times.

문헌.ex: 이 내용은 조선 시대 문헌에 기록되어 있어요.
문헌.x: This is recorded in documents from the Joseon era.
문헌.e: Originally 'writings and wise men' as sources of knowledge; now any written source.
문헌.t: 참고 문헌 means 'references' or 'bibliography' in a paper.

수반하다.m: to accompany, to entail, to involve
수반하다.ex: 새로운 사업은 언제나 큰 위험을 수반합니다.
수반하다.x: A new business always involves great risk.
수반하다.t: Often passive-like: 고통이 수반되다 (pain is involved); it means a natural consequence comes along.

불허하다.x: The police refused to allow the group's rally.
불허하다.t: Set phrase: 예측을 불허하다 or 예측 불허 'unpredictable,' common in sports news.

초지일관.m: sticking to one's original intention, consistency
초지일관.ex: 그는 초지일관 환경 보호를 위해 일했어요.
초지일관.x: He worked consistently for environmental protection, true to his original goal.
초지일관.e: Literally 'carry the first intention straight through'.

정정당당.m: fair and square; open and aboveboard
정정당당.x: All the athletes swore to compete fair and square.
정정당당.t: Usually 정정당당하다 or 정정당당하게; famous from the athletes' oath at sports events.

잔금.ex: 계약금은 냈고 잔금은 다음 달에 내기로 했어요.
잔금.x: I've paid the deposit, and I'll pay the balance next month.

알선.m: mediation, arranging, brokering; (law) acting as a go-between
알선.ex: 이 센터는 외국인 노동자에게 일자리를 알선해 줍니다.
알선.x: This center arranges jobs for foreign workers.
알선.e: Literally 'turning around': going between two parties to arrange a deal.

출자.m: capital contribution, investment (in a company as an owner)
출자.ex: 두 회사가 절반씩 출자해서 새 회사를 세웠습니다.
출자.x: The two companies each put in half the capital and set up a new company.
출자.t: 출자 means putting money in as an owner; 투자 is the broader word for any investment.

정족수.ex: 의원들이 많이 빠져서 정족수를 채우지 못했어요.
정족수.x: So many lawmakers were absent that they couldn't reach a quorum.
정족수.t: Common phrases: 정족수를 채우다 (reach a quorum) and 정족수 미달 (lacking a quorum).

권위주의.ex: 그 나라는 권위주의 정권에서 민주주의로 바뀌었습니다.
권위주의.x: That country changed from an authoritarian regime to a democracy.
권위주의.t: 권위적이다 also describes bossy people: 권위적인 상사 is an authoritarian boss.

귀화.ex: 그는 한국으로 귀화해서 국가대표 선수가 됐어요.
귀화.x: He became a naturalized Korean citizen and joined the national team.
귀화.e: Literally 'turning and coming over' to another country's rule.
귀화.t: Pattern: (나라)로 귀화하다 — 한국으로 귀화하다 (become a naturalized Korean).

자비.ex: 부처님의 자비는 모든 생명에게 미친다고 해요.
자비.x: The Buddha's compassion is said to reach all living beings.
자비.e: Literally 'loving-kindness and sorrow': sharing others' joy and pain.
자비.t: A homonym 자비 means 'one's own expense', as in 자비로 출판하다 (to self-publish).

효제.x: The Analects says filial piety and brotherly respect are the root of benevolence.
효제.e: Respect for parents plus respect for older siblings.

연구윤리.x: Every researcher must follow research ethics.
연구윤리.t: Pronounced [연구율리] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

설치미술.ex: 전시장 한가운데에 거대한 설치미술 작품이 놓여 있었어요.
설치미술.x: A huge installation art piece stood in the middle of the exhibition hall.

미사여구.ex: 미사여구만 늘어놓지 말고 핵심을 말해 주세요.
미사여구.x: Don't just string together fancy words; get to the point.
미사여구.t: Usually negative: 미사여구를 늘어놓다 'to pile on flowery words' without substance.

궐기하다.m: to rise up, to rally (in protest)
궐기하다.x: Citizens rose up against the rigged election.
궐기하다.e: Literally 'spring to one's feet': rising up together for a cause.

매료되다.m: to be fascinated, to be captivated, to be charmed
매료되다.x: The audience was completely captivated by her voice.

조촐하다.x: We had a small, simple birthday party with just the family.
조촐하다.t: Common with gatherings and meals: 조촐한 식사, 조촐한 결혼식.
